svg.text: Stage 2 wiring: LED ring (after the sensors work)
Every orange 5V tag connects together, and every black GND tag connects together: use the breadboard's two long power rails.
Use the COM / UART port (normally the left one; the label is on the back).
Check: Windows Device Manager shows "USB-SERIAL CH343".
top view · notch up · dot = pin 1
D1: ESP32 GPIO4 (left header, pin 4) → chip pin 2 (1A)
D2: chip pin 3 (1Y) → 330 Ω → strip DIN
WS2812B strip around the ring · data flows left to right (printed arrows point away from the input)
1000 µF capacitor at the INPUT end:
long leg to 5V, striped leg to GND.
18 AWG from the rails to BOTH strip ends
• The ESP32 is powered only by its own USB-C (COM port). The LED supply never connects to the ESP32's 5Vin or 3V3.
• The LED supply's GND and the ESP32's GND are joined (the GND rail). Without this the data signal does not work.
• Solder to the strip's INPUT end (printed arrows point away from it). Feed 5V and GND at the far end too.
• Chip goes in the breadboard across the centre gap, notch up; pin 1 is top-left, next to the dot.
